correctness.rationale: Every rectangle is counted once by the two columns belonging to its row-pair/color slot. Each column contributes at least four slot incidences, with equality at weights two and three. Pairwise balancing of integer loads proves R≥20 binom(q,2)+4qr at b=5q+r. When b=5q is odd, an unbalanced column adds at least two incidences and hence at least 2q to this bound. Otherwise the sum of deviations from q is zero and the defect is one-half the sum of their squares. An independent form of the parity argument: let e_i be the parity of ones in row i; then the number s_ij of same-color agreements is odd precisely when e_i=e_j, since b is odd. At least four of the ten pairs are within the two parity classes (the minimum is the 2+3 split). Each odd pair forces at least one nonzero integer deviation, so defect ≥2. Independently recomputed the B, C, W slot histograms as {2:20}, {0:4,1:16}, {0:2,1:16,2:2}. In B the two-one masks form a 5-cycle and the two-zero masks its complement; regularity explains the uniform loads. C is a subset of B with no repeated slot. W has exactly two rectangles, from mask pairs (24,12) and (24,18). Add copies of B, append a prefix of C or remove it from the next copy, or append W at residue five; the corresponding distributions give the stated equality and exceptional defect for all widths, including b<5. Independent direct counts through width 120 are supporting checks rather than the universal proof.
residual_risks: Two labeled colors and repeated columns are permitted; the theorem is an optimum count, not a classification or enumeration of all minimizers.
